title: Returning to pleasure by choice
meaning: Returning to a familiar pleasure can enliven your time together when agreement is free from the need to prove closeness.
text: Shared enjoyment can have a second beginning. Judgement in the physical position of Svadhisthana suggests returning to something that could bring pleasure and giving it a fresh voice today. The Lovers in energy describe a vulnerable expectation here: a shared wish must confirm again that you choose each other. Justice in emotions experiences enjoyment through fairness of choice, with a need to know that nobody agreed merely from duty. A simple invitation can acquire more meaning than it can comfortably carry.

Imagine suggesting that you learn a song together just for your own enjoyment. “Let's do it another day” can easily sound like a lack of interest in all your shared time. **Revived pleasure comes alive through free agreement, rather than proof of closeness.** Each person can reach desire at a different pace even when the idea matters to both. Agreeing on a suitable moment gives the invitation more clarity than checking feelings again.

The difficulty begins when reciprocity is measured through equal readiness right now. To restore fairness, comparisons appear: who suggests things more often, and who postpones them? Leisure becomes an account of contributions to the relationship. Your shared enjoyment has more room to return when a small “I don't feel like it today” remains an answer about this particular evening.
